hints.content:
First, let’s look at the hourly rate for the lifeguard job.  On Monday, it pays $\$54.00$ for $\pink6$ hours worked, so  the hourly rate is 

$\dfrac{\$54.00}{\pink6\,\, \text{hours}}= \$9.00$ per hour.

Similarly, we see that on Tuesday, the job pays an hourly rate of

$\dfrac{\$36.00}{\blue4\,\,\text{hours}}=\$9.00$ per hour, 

and on Wednesday it pays 

$\dfrac{\$72.00}{\green8\,\,\text{hours}}=\$9.00$ per hour. 

 So the lifeguard job pays  $\$9.00$ per hour, which is more than the camp counselor job.
**The lifeguard job pays a higher hourly rate.**

question.content:
Jason has applied for two summer jobs, one as a lifeguard and the other as a camp counselor.  The lifeguard job is three days a week, and pays the following as shown in the table below (the pay rate is the same on each of the three days).

The camp counselor job pays $\$8.75$ per hour.  

**Which job pays a higher hourly rate?**

 |Monday|Tuesday|Wednesday
-:|-:|-:|-:
Hours worked|$6$|$4$|$8$
Amount paid|$\$54.00$|$\$36.00$|$\$72.00$

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.content: The two jobs pay at the same rate.
